question:
A nucleus of mass $M\approx 200u$ emits a single $\gamma$ photon of energy $E_\gamma=2.00\,\text{MeV}$.

In a separate atomic process, a hydrogen electron makes a transition from $n=5$ to $n=2$, emitting a photon of energy $E_{52}$.

(a) Calculate $E_{52}$.

(b) Let $N$ be the number of $5\to2$ photons needed to carry the same total energy as one $2.00\,\text{MeV}$ $\gamma$ photon.

(c) Compare the recoil kinetic energy of the nucleus in two cases:

- Case I: one $2.00\,\text{MeV}$ $\gamma$ photon emitted.
- Case II: $N$ photons each of energy $E_{52}$ emitted in random directions. Assume the average resultant momentum is $p_{\text{net}}\approx \sqrt{N}\,\dfrac{E_{52}}{c}$.

Use $E_n=-\dfrac{13.6}{n^2}\,\text{eV}$ and $1u\,c^2=931.5\,\text{MeV}$.
